S106.13.needs: a Slack workspace where you can add apps, the Slack app set up by the owner first (see the code note)
S106.13.note: The Slack reply happens inside Slack, not in the AGI screens; the code marks this item unfinished until the owner creates the Slack app and applies migration 0333; the way into Settings from the first screen was not located in the code.
steps: Open Settings and choose Slack app under Customize.
In the card Slack workspaces you added, click Add to Slack, and finish the install on Slack's own page.
In Slack, open a direct message with the AGI app and send a message such as hello.
Look at the DM: the assistant's reply should appear in that same DM, and compare it with Expected.
S106.13.where: Settings > Customize > Slack app > Slack workspaces you added > Add to Slack, then message AGI in Slack

S106.14.needs: a Slack workspace where you can add apps and invite them to a channel, the Slack app set up by the owner first
S106.14.note: The channel reply and action happen in Slack; the owner must create the Slack app and apply migration 0333 first, and the code is marked partial.
steps: Open Settings, choose Slack app under Customize, and read the card Slack workspaces you added: it says to add the app, then /invite it to channels.
In Slack, type /invite and the app name in a channel to add the app to that channel.
Post a normal message in that channel and wait for the agent to act.
Check the channel for the agent's reply, and check Settings > Customize > Slack app > Waiting for your approval for any request, then compare with Expected.
S106.14.where: Settings > Customize > Slack app > Slack workspaces you added (read the text there), then in Slack use /invite in a channel

labels.text: A task from a channel mention

S106.16.needs: a Slack channel where the app is invited, the Slack app set up by the owner first
S106.16.note: The task is listed in that card only when the run needs approval; the link View task appears only when a task path exists, and where the task shows otherwise was not confirmed in the code.
steps: In a Slack channel where the app is invited, write a message that mentions the app with a request.
In AGI, open Settings > Customize > Slack app and look at the card Waiting for your approval.
Find the item that says A task from a channel mention, and click View task if it appears.
Compare with Expected: the channel message should now be a task the agent runs.
S106.16.where: In Slack, @mention the app in a channel message; then in AGI open Settings > Customize > Slack app > Waiting for your approval

S106.21.needs: a Slack workspace where the app is installed and a Slack account of your own, the Slack app set up by the owner first
S106.21.note: The bot identity is shown by Slack, and the code that sets it was not checked against Slack's display; the item is marked partial in the code.
steps: Open Settings, choose Slack app under Customize, and read the card Your Slack accounts: it says accounts AGI answers as you.
In Slack, mention the app in a channel with a short request.
Read the reply in Slack and compare its sender name with your own name.
Compare with Expected: the agent should answer under its own app identity, not as you.
S106.21.where: Settings > Customize > Slack app > Your Slack accounts; the agent's own name is seen in Slack

S106.24.needs: a paid account with at least one schedule that has run
S106.24.note: The sidebar label for the Scheduled page was not found in the code; whether channel runs appear in this list was not confirmed by reading the code.
steps: Open the Scheduled page.
On a schedule card, click the history icon button (its tooltip says Run History).
Read the section Run History that opens under the card.
Compare with Expected: work started from a channel or host should be listed there for review.
S106.24.where: Scheduled page (route /chat/schedules, page title Scheduled) > schedule card > Run History button
